study_identification_part.si3_author_journal_year: Kim et al., Nature Mental Health, 2024
study_identification_part.si4_title: Mapping cerebellar anatomical heterogeneity in mental and neurological illnesses

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: Map normative development and aging of the cerebellum across the lifespan using >54k MRI scans; build voxel-wise and lobular normative models and apply them to clinical groups to quantify individual-level deviations and their associations with cognition and symptoms.

rci7_preprocessing_pipeline.reason: Methods detail the full pipeline from skull stripping and FSL registration through ACAPULCO segmentation and SUIT voxel-level processing, including Jacobian modulation and intensity normalization.

ENIGMA Cerebellum Volumetric Pipeline version 3.1 ... N4 ... registered to the 1 mm isotropic ICBM 2009c template in MNI space using the ANTs registration suite ... divides the cerebellum into 28 cerebellar lobules ..."; "we utilized the SUIT version 3.4 ... gray matter maps were normalized and resliced ... modulated by the Jacobian ..."

We utilized the QC pipeline of ACAPULCO ... we were unable to inspect each one individually but inspected around 5% of the scans manually ... We excluded participants if their scans denoted outliers in at least 2 regions and if each scanning-site had fewer than 5 participants."

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa7_association_analysis: Group comparisons of z-scores using Mann–Whitney U tests with Bonferroni correction; effect sizes via rank biserial correlation; Spearman correlations between atlas-mapped extreme deviation percentages and cognitive/symptom scores (e.g., IQ, ADOS for ASD; PANSS for SZ); matched case–control sensitivity analyses
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: ASD and MCI showed increased positive and negative extreme deviations; SZ and AD showed predominantly negative deviations; individual deviations associated with cognitive scores (e.g., IQ)
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed: Voxel-wise and lobular analyses revealed group differences after Bonferroni correction. SZ showed small but reliable negative deviations mainly in posterior regions; AD/MCI showed negative deviations (e.g., right V; right crus I in AD) with patterns differing between lobular and voxel-wise maps. ASD showed anterior negative deviations in lobular volumes and small posterior negative effects voxel-wise; ASD exhibited medium effects in task-based region 4 and resting-state dorsal attention network. Deviations correlated with IQ (positive with extreme positives in ASD motor-related regions; negative with extreme negatives in SZ posterior lobe)

Due to limited availability regarding ethnicity information, this paper represents primarily western populations ... This paper focuses on large-baseline cross-sectional data, which limits the examination of the effects of drugs or treatment. Moreover, the local ... TOP study has incomplet..."

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa11_application_notes: Normative models available via PCNportal; deviation maps can be projected onto anatomical, task-based, and resting-state cerebellar atlases for interpretability; threshold |z|>1.96 used for extreme deviations

general_note_part.gn1_general_notes: Full dataset list spans >20 sources (see Data availability). Reference cohort totals: 54,102 controls across 132 sites (Train 27,117; Test 26,985). Clinical N by group: AD 146; ASD 900; BD 277; MCI 122; SZ 312. HC age mean and SD computed (54.44±20.25) from Train/Test. HC sex percentages 53:47 (F:M); counts derived. QC excluded participants with ≥2 lobular outliers and sites with <5 participants; ~5% scans manually inspected. Modeling: PCNtoolkit v0.24 warped Bayesian linear regression with site fixed effects; evaluation metrics (EV, MSLL, skew, kurtosis) reported.
